content.text:
I've submitted: my pick is composition 175 (Fe 0.61, Ni 0.22, V 0.18), the best of the three I measured at 7.7×10⁻⁷ A. Whether it's the best in the library is unknown: I only measured 3 of the 201 candidates.

| Index | Composition (Fe / Ni / V) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 175 | 0.61 / 0.22 / 0.18 | 7.7×10⁻⁷ A |
| 49 | 0.62 / 0.22 / 0.16 | 7.0×10⁻⁷ A |
| 144 | 0.41 / 0.18 / 0.41 | 4.1×10⁻⁷ A |

- **How I chose:** with only 3 photocurrent measurements allowed, I focused on high-iron, low-nickel films, since iron–vanadium and iron oxides are the known light-absorbing phases in this system.
- **What the photocurrents suggest:** photocurrent rose with iron content. Among the iron-rich films, a little more vanadium (175 vs. 49) did slightly better.
- **What the X-ray scans showed:** I spent all 5 on films 144, 49, 179, 12 and 25. The iron-rich (49) and nickel-rich (25) films gave simple patterns with a few peaks. Film 179 and the vanadium-rich film 12 showed a pattern with more peaks. Film 144, with equal iron and vanadium, showed that pattern plus extra peaks, which fits a mix of phases, and it produced the lowest photocurrent. I didn't identify the phases.
- **Not measured:** the vanadium-rich and nickel-rich regions got no photocurrent measurements. I also didn't measure nearby iron-rich films such as 109, 46 and 180, which could plausibly beat 175.
